pharm: Concentration-dependent bactericidal aminoglycoside; semisynthetic kanamycin derivative with Gram-negative coverage including Pseudomonas.
summary: Semisynthetic aminoglycoside for short-term treatment of serious Gram-negative infections, including Pseudomonas. Given IM or IV (not orally absorbed). Carries boxed warnings for ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity; requires renal dosing, serum level monitoring, and audiometry. Therapy usually limited to 7-14 days.
indications: Short-term treatment of serious Gram-negative infections (Pseudomonas, E. coli, Proteus, Klebsiella-Enterobacter-Serratia, Acinetobacter)
Complicated and recurrent urinary tract infections

dosage.n: Max 15 mg/kg/day; total adult dose not to exceed 1.5 g/day
Common clinical practice; maximizes concentration-dependent killing
Adjust per renal function and serum levels
Avoid dosing on total body weight

admin: Administer IM or by IV infusion; not absorbed orally
IV: dilute and infuse over 30-60 minutes (adults); 1-2 hours in infants
Do not mix with beta-lactam antibiotics in the same syringe or line (mutual inactivation)
Usual duration 7-10 days; safety beyond 14 days not established
moa: Binds irreversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit, causing misreading of mRNA and inhibition of bacterial protein synthesis; concentration-dependent bactericidal activity against aerobic Gram-negative bacilli.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to amikacin or other aminoglycosides

preg: Aminoglycosides cross the placenta and may cause congenital deafness/ototoxicity; avoid unless life-threatening infection (former category D).
lact: Small amounts excreted in breast milk; minimal oral absorption by the infant; use with caution.
renal: Requires dose adjustment - reduce dose or extend interval based on CrCl and serum levels; renal excretion is the major route of elimination.

major: Other nephrotoxic/ototoxic drugs (other aminoglycosides, vancomycin, amphotericin B, cisplatin, cyclosporine)
Potent diuretics (furosemide, ethacrynic acid) - enhance ototoxicity
Neuromuscular blockers and anesthetics - potentiate neuromuscular blockade with risk of respiratory paralysis
moderate: NSAIDs - reduce clearance, especially in neonates
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum peak and trough levels; do not mix with beta-lactams in the same syringe (inactivation).

serious: Ototoxicity (hearing loss, often irreversible; tinnitus; vertigo)

monitoring: Renal function (serum creatinine, BUN, urine output) before and during therapy
Serum calcium, magnesium, sodium, and potassium
counsel: Report any hearing changes, ringing in the ears, or dizziness immediately
This is a short-course hospital antibiotic given by injection
Inform your clinician of any kidney problems or other ear/kidney-affecting medications
pk: IM ~0.5-2 h (~30-90 min post-dose); IV at end of infusion
~2-3 h; greatly prolonged in renal impairment (up to 30-86 h in anuria)
20-25 C; do not use if discolored
pearls: Extended-interval (once-daily) dosing maximizes concentration-dependent killing and post-antibiotic effect while reducing toxicity
Trough level is the key safety marker for toxicity
Not absorbed orally - must be given parenterally
Synergistic with beta-lactams but never mix in the same line
missed: Hospital-administered; give as soon as noted and adjust the schedule. Do not double the dose. Recheck serum levels if timing is altered.
overdose: Remove drug with hemodialysis (effective) or peritoneal dialysis; provide supportive care. For neuromuscular blockade, give calcium salts or anticholinesterase agents, or use mechanical ventilation. Monitor renal and auditory function.
